assessments.reasoning: The title page identifies the authors and the JKU publication record connects this author copy to the 1991 paper. Fresh HTTP 200 yielded the retained complete PDF, SHA-256 8812e21426954c0e17100bd0e3f2ce0a5c24b8ef6cc8dbddb0bff12fdf8848e7. Checked page streams and rendered page witnesses. Printed p. 16 (physical PDF p. 16), §10.2, redefinition and procedure selection paragraphs and the Insert example; printed p. 21 (physical PDF p. 21), Appendix A, Matching formal parameter lists. The three paragraphs after the productions explain inheritance and redefinition, dynamic procedure selection, and the dedicated base binding. Appendix A defines matching lists. The ordinary selection can resolve to a different binding from one selected by the static type. The caret example reaches the inherited binding explicitly. For redefinition the formal parameter lists must match. When the inherited procedure and extension type are exported, the redefinition must also be exported. The caret form is scoped to a receiver parameter and its base-type procedure binding. This describes rule-level selection in the named report. Dispatch implementation, layout and error behavior require additional evidence. Base selection has a receiver-specific rule. Ordinary field selection, pointer dereferencing and static visibility remain separate issues.
